sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 7.7% a year from $15.4 billion in FY2018 to $25.8 billion in FY2025 [F1][F8][F145], but operating income grew faster at 9.9% [F146] while net income was flat at 0.4% [F147].
The window is not a smooth compounder: operating margin swung from 30.6% in FY2019 [F18] to 15.5% in FY2021 [F20] and back to 41.3% in FY2023 [F22], a 25.8pp range around a 30.3% median [D300].

The FY2021 trough reflected a $1.5 billion Mountain Valley Pipeline impairment and unfavorable non-qualifying hedge activity at NEER [P63][P68], while the FY2023 peak reflected $1.7 billion of non-qualifying hedge gains at NEER [P30].
FY2024 revenue fell 5.2% [D201] on lower storm and fuel cost recovery revenues at FPL [P35], and FY2025 recovered 9.8% [D236] on higher storm cost recovery and retail base revenues [P21].
FPL is the dominant revenue line at 70.5% of FY2025 revenue [D271], down from 76.5% in FY2020 [D258], and contributed 5.5pp of the 9.8% FY2025 growth [D273][D236].
FPL's FY2025 revenue increase came from higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan revenues, partly offset by lower fuel cost recovery [P21].
NEER's FY2025 results rose on higher earnings from new investments, with 1,604 MW of wind, 2,859 MW of solar and 1,799 MW of battery storage added [P26].
Operating income grew 10.7% in FY2025 against 9.8% revenue growth [D237][D236], an incremental margin of 34.8% [D256], but operating costs grew 10.0% versus revenue's 9.8% [D249][D236].
Diluted EPS fell 2.1% in FY2025 [D240] against a 1.6% net income decline [D238], with the diluted share count up 0.6% [D251].
FY2025 operating margin of 32.1% [F24] sits 1.8pp above the 30.3% window median [D300] and well below the 41.3% FY2023 high [D299], but far above the 15.5% FY2021 low [D298].
The FY2025 margin was essentially flat, up 0.3pp [D247], as D&A rose to 25.5% of revenue [D224] and operating expenses grew 10.0% [D249].
D&A increased $951 million in FY2025, mainly higher amortization of deferred storm costs for Hurricanes Debby, Helene and Milton plus higher plant in service [P16].
Net margin fell 3.1pp to 26.5% [F40][D248] even as operating margin held, because other income (expense) was -$3.75 billion [X64] and the effective tax rate was -17.7% [D226].
Corporate and Other's results fell $1.26 billion, largely on $1.0 billion of unfavorable non-qualifying hedge activity and higher average debt balances [P8].
Operating cash flow of $12.5 billion [F64] was 1.83x net income in FY2025 [D227], in line with the 1.55x-2.73x range across the window [D157][D52].
Operating cash flow fell 5.8% in FY2025 [D241] and was 48.4% of revenue [D225], while investing outflow reached $23.9 billion [F72].
The swing from net over-recovery to net under-recovery of cost recovery clauses cut FPL's operating cash flow by about $89 million in FY2025 [P19].
Stock-based compensation is immaterial to cash at 1.5% of operating cash flow [D228], so conversion is driven by working capital and the capital programme, not equity pay.
Net debt deepened to $92.2 billion in FY2025 [D231] from $34.3 billion in FY2018 [D9], with long-term debt compounding at 18.8% [F156] against equity's 6.9% [F157].
Net cash is -357.4% of revenue [D232], the 0th percentile against four utilities peers whose median is -228.4% [D314][D315], so leverage is heavier than the group.
Liquidity is thin: the current ratio is 0.60x [F128], the window high [D305] but still below 1.0x, with working capital of -$9.23 billion [F120].

Free cash flow is negative after $23.9 billion of investing outflow [F72], funded by $23.4 billion of debt issued [X90] and $13.0 billion of net financing [F80], while dividends of $4.68 billion [X82] were paid and the share count rose 0.6% [D251].
The current ratio has stayed below 1.0x every year of the window, at 0.60x in FY2025 [F128], so the flag is structural for a capital-intensive utility rather than new [R1].
Net cash has deteriorated for seven straight years, from -$34.3 billion in FY2018 to -$92.2 billion in FY2025 [D9][D231], as debt growth outran cash generation [R2].
The FY2025 effective tax rate of -17.7% [D226] reflects clean energy tax credits at NEER, which rose about $585 million [P11], so the low rate is policy-driven and could reverse [R4].
FY2019 operating expenses were later restated to $14.3 billion from the $13.9 billion first reported [X18][R5], a data-quality caveat on that year's margin comparison.
Operating margin: a print below the 30.3% window median [D300] in the FY2026 10-K would confirm the FY2023 peak was hedge-driven rather than structural.
Net cash: further deterioration past the FY2025 level of -$92.2 billion [D231] in the FY2026 10-K would extend the seven-year trend and pressure the dividend funded at $4.68 billion [X82].
Operating cash flow conversion: a ratio below the FY2025 1.83x [D227] in the FY2026 10-K would signal working-capital or cost-recovery strain.
